key_insight: Well-calibrated large language models can act as low-cost statistical estimators that achieve Bayes-optimal risk for inference tasks depending only on conditional means under squared loss.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical substitute for expensive human-subject experiments in decision pipelines when the target quantity is a conditional expectation and the model is within its valid scope.
method: Model the LLM as a misspecified functional estimator trained on i.i.d. data.
Decompose error into representation bias and optimization error, then bound asymptotic risk with regularity conditions.
Use bidirectional Le Cam deficiency plus a calibration protocol to establish restricted functional risk equivalence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical risk analysis, finite-sample concentration bounds, and calibration decision rules rather than a new empirical benchmark.
watch_item: Performance depends on the task being conditional-mean-based and on proper calibration; identifiability error can raise the effective bias and risk floor.
paper_title: Using Large Language Models as Low-Cost Statistical Estimators for Human-Response Data
